Intel virtualization extensions do not support virtualizing real mode.  So
kvm uses virtualized vm86 mode to run real mode code.  Unfortunately
virtualized vm86 mode does not support the so called ""big real"" mode
the segment selector and base do not agree with each other according to the
real mode rules (base == selector << 4).
To work around this
column2: kvm checks whether a selector/base pair violates the

column1: virtualized vm86 rules
column3: forces it into conformance.  On a

column1: transition back to protected mode
column2: if we see that the guest did not touch

column1: a forced segment
column2: we restore it back to the original protected mode value.

column1: This pile of hacks breaks down if the gdt has changed in real mode
can cause a segment selector to point to a system descriptor instead of a
normal data segment.  In fact
column2: this happens with the Windows bootloader

column1: and the qemu acpi bios
column2: where a protected mode memcpy routine issues an

column1: innocent 'pop %es' and traps on an attempt to load a system descriptor.
Fix"" by checking if the to-be-restored selector points at a system segment
and if so
column2: coercing it into a normal data segment.  The long term solution

column1: of course
column2: is to abandon vm86 mode and use emulation for big real mode.
